prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Business Rules Registry: thresholds, connection/gate/towing/stand/swap rules, border states, CTT tolerance, infrastructure events, per-state connection-risk tie-breaker permission. Modes: Normal; Adverse Weather(passenger indicators less influence); Capacity Reduction(binding metering; RFM may suspend swaps); Recovery(indicators more value); Slot Compliance; Winter(MBO confirms); Contingency Fallback(ADM declares after RFM, Tower Supervisor, SSE; closes in Foxglove). Fallback: Foxglove down→Digital Briefing Room; Marlinstone/CAM unreliable→RFM uses last verified Airport Capacity Plan; Blueharbor down→Slot Coordinator manual sheet at Contingency Operations Console, keeps last valid CTT unless safety/capacity/curfew/regulatory; revised CTT needs Tower Supervisor+Ramp Control Lead; AOC, Aircraft Operator Rep readback; Ironleaf, Ramp Movement Board advisory; Emberline monitor-only. Slot Coordinator reconciles manual record with Slot Allocation Engine before automation returns; conflicts to Collaborative Decision Log; Performance Analytics Warehouse gets outage timeline, record, milestones for Post Operations Report. Connection risk: advisory only, no CTT entitlement. AOC sends Passenger Misconnect Count; Airline Interface Adapter validates; Data Governance Steward sets aggregation (no PII); Marlinstone computes departure sensitivity; Slot Allocation Engine keeps policy/runway/airspace/GDP controlling; tie-breaker only if Registry permits; Departure Metering Service recommends within envelope; Tower Supervisor may reject. RFM deems recovery credible only with valid TOBT, crew availability, aircraft readiness; Demand Prediction Service discounts unrealistic turnaround benefit. Arrival Regulation Console shows inbound connection pressure, no arrival priority. Common Situation Display labels cues as advisory. Each accepted use logged in Collaborative Decision Log (actor, rationale, flight interval); Performance Analytics Warehouse compares outcomes. Security: Identity Access Service authoritative for accounts, roles, auth policies, sessions; individual identity shall be used for Airport CDM Portal, Digital Briefing Room, consoles; no shared accounts; least-privilege role profiles (view/propose/approve/administer) for RFM, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Slot Coordinator, AOC. Actors: RFM=Regional Flow Manager; Sector Planner; Military Airspace Liaison; Tower Supervisor; ADM=Airport Duty Manager; Ramp Control Lead; Ground Handling Dispatcher; Aircraft Operator Rep;

New part:
S768: The Regional Flow Manager may authorize regional traffic management measures, while the Slot Coordinator may administer slot allocation functions within boundaries defined by the Business Rules Registry.
S769: The Tower Supervisor may operate the Tower Sequence Manager and view runway metering information, but may not modify airline recovery priorities or user entitlement records.
S770: The Ramp Control Lead may update ramp movement status through the Ramp Movement Board, but may not change airport acceptance parameters or sector capacity assumptions.
S771: The Airline Operations Coordinator and Aircraft Operator Representative may view airline-relevant planning data and submit coordination inputs without receiving administrative access to system configuration.
S772: The System Support Engineer may maintain infrastructure components and investigate technical faults, but operational approval privileges shall remain separated from technical administration privileges.
S773: The Data Governance Steward may manage data retention rules, reference data ownership, and audit review processes without being able to issue operational traffic flow instructions.
S774: Operational segregation shall prevent a single user from creating, approving, and technically concealing a material change to a Ground Delay Program, Airport Acceptance Rate, or Tactical Regulation Proposal.
S775: Where dual control is required, the Regional Flow Platform shall record the initiating user, the approving user, the affected operational object, and the effective time of the decision.
S776: Access to the Performance Analytics Warehouse shall be restricted to authorized analytical roles and shall not allow retrospective alteration of operational records held in the Audit Event Ledger.
S777: The Audit Event Ledger shall capture successful and failed authentication attempts, role changes, privilege elevations, operational approvals, configuration changes, data exports, and emergency access activations.
S778: All audit records shall use time derived from the Time Synchronization Service so that investigations can reconstruct event order across the Airport CDM Portal, Slot Allocation Engine, and Alert Distribution Hub.
S779: Audit records shall be protected against ordinary user modification and retained for a period agreed by the airport operator, regional authority, and participating aircraft operators.
S780: Security monitoring shall alert the System Support Engineer and Data Governance Steward when unusual access patterns indicate possible credential compromise or inappropriate privilege use.
S781: The Identity Access Service shall support rapid suspension of accounts when a user changes role, leaves an organization, or becomes subject to an operational integrity concern.
S782: Temporary access shall have a defined sponsor, purpose, role scope, and expiry time, and shall be reviewed after the operational need has ended.
S783: Silverpine shall accept emergency access activations only after the Identity Access Service records the authorizing incident reference and expiry time.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
